North Korean hackers used fake video calls in $400m crypto hack, says FBI
- Published
State-sponsored hackers from North Korea have taken more than $400 million in cryptocurrency by using fake video calls to steal people's identities, US authorities say.
More than 900 victims have fallen prey to the scheme, which the FBI refers to as FaceStealer, in the last 18 months, according to the bureau.
"The North Korean regime relies on proceeds from large-scale cryptocurrency theft to fund its illicit weapons program, stealing billions of dollars in recent years," says FBI cyber director Brett Leatherman.
This comes a week after the world's largest crypto exchange Binance revealed that hackers had used fake job interviews to steal a record $6.3bn (£4.7bn) from the company.
US law enforcement agencies attributed the Binance hack, thought to be the largest crypto hack to date, to North Korea-linked actors. Pyongyang has denied this claim.
Authorities say FaceStealer, the latest scheme, "aggressively targets" those who work in the cryptocurrency and web3 sectors, particularly those who are involved in the development and maintenance of open-source software.
According to the FBI and US Justice Department, FaceStealer hackers use fake or hijacked social media accounts to invite potential victims into video calls hosted over "imposter versions" of Zoom, Microsoft Teams, and Google Meet.
Next, the hackers play pre-recorded videos of previous victims the target is acquainted with to simulate a legitimate call – except that the audio would appear to malfunction.
A message then pops up on the target's screen, asking them to "fix" the audio by clicking on a link. This "fix" would eventually download malware onto the target's device, which allows hackers to access their contact lists and apps, widening their pool of potential victims.
Hackers would secretly record these calls and use the recordings as material to scam their new victims, according to the US authorities.
The FBI has described FaceStealer as "a highly effective social engineering scheme capable of deceiving even the most experienced technical and security conscious computer user".
"It exploits our trust in ubiquitous video conference platforms and valued personal relationships," Patrick Grandy, assistant director in charge of the bureau's Los Angeles field office, said in a statement on Thursday.
"If you can't imagine a scenario where you might fall prey to it, you are not thinking creatively enough."

Bhopal (Madhya Pradesh): After the Directorate of Medical Education (DME) submitted a reply in the High Court over double advantage to in-service candidates, the High Court has not vacated the stay on the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test for Postgraduate (NEET PG) counselling. Medical officers posted in such areas discharge their duties in challenging conditions, often without the facilities and professional exposure ordinarily available in urban institutions.

U.S. envoys meet with Putin in the Kremlin after Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi
MOSCOW — U.S. President Donald Trump's envoys met Thursday with President Vladimir Putin as Washington sought new momentum in peace efforts after two days of U.S.-mediated negotiations between Russian and Ukrainian delegations.
Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, who is also Trump's son-in-law, brokered the talks in Abu Dhabi, the capital of the United Arab Emirates. Those were the first direct discussions between representatives of Moscow and Kyiv in nine months as the push for peace stalled.
The two days of talks that ended Wednesday produced no major breakthrough, aside from an agreement to swap a large number of prisoners, with the exact figure still to be announced.
Kushner and Witkoff went straight to the Kremlin to brief Putin in a meeting that lasted about two hours and are scheduled to fly to Dublin, Ireland, for talks with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy as the conflict stretches toward the five-year mark.
U.S. envoys want Europe at the negotiating table, too
Kushner said that one of the goals of the meeting with Putin was to get the Russian leader's blessing for European representatives to be part of the talks, which are looking at the continent's broader security arrangements.
The U.S. and Zelenskyy want Europe to appoint a single person to negotiate with Moscow.
But Moscow doesn't want European countries involved in the direct negotiations, complaining they are financing and supplying Ukraine's military effort. The Europeans are concerned about Russia's conduct and broader intentions on the continent.
Many in Europe see the inclusion of Moscow in discussions about postwar European security as an unwelcome concession to Putin, who has described NATO's eastward expansion as a main security threat to Russia. Putin has demanded the trans-Atlantic alliance's troops be pulled back from Russia's borders.
Some analysts say negotiators may be looking to grant Russia concessions on NATO's strategy in return for peace in Ukraine — a possibility that alarms European leaders.
The Russian and Ukrainian delegations in Abu Dhabi "agreed on many of the principles, but are still apart on some of the way to accomplish" peace, Kushner said in Moscow.
Putin reaffirmed to the U.S. envoys that any European troops sent to Ukraine after a ceasefire would be "absolutely unacceptable" and Russia would regard the deployment as a security threat and legitimate targets. "In other words, the war would resume immediately," he said.
He also said Russia regards its border with Ukraine to be sealed by a prospective peace deal as now extending to cover the four Ukrainian regions that Moscow annexed in 2022 but never fully controlled.
Zelenskyy sees a political "window of opportunity"
Zelenskyy is in Dublin for a meeting of more than 40 European countries that also includes NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte.
Rutte said the U.S., Europe and Ukraine are "very much aligned" on what security guarantees should look like, following a meeting in Paris in January. "But now of course we need the peace deal, or at least a ceasefire," Rutte said.
Zelenskyy said political changes, including Democrats taking over the U.S. Congress in January following midterm elections and balloting in France next year, could bring "a window of opportunity" for a peace deal.
"The political landscape in Europe could change in 2027. … We also see changes already taking place in the United States," Zelenskyy said in Dublin late Wednesday.
He called the proposed prisoner exchange a positive step but also insisted Ukraine won't surrender Russian-occupied territory in return for peace.
Russia and Ukraine have occasionally swapped prisoners, but both sides remain far apart in their terms for accepting a settlement.
Fighting continues as another bitter winter approaches
Amid the negotiations, fighting continues along the 1,200-kilometer (about 750-mile) front line.
Russia's bigger army has been held back by dogged Ukrainian resistance while Moscow's drone and missile strikes on Ukraine's energy facilities disrupted heat, electricity and water supplies to Ukrainian cities, sapping public morale in what Kyiv calls a "weaponization of winter."
Russia's Defense Ministry said its air defenses downed 71 Ukrainian drones overnight. Its forces struck a drone-manufacturing plant in Kyiv and three other facilities producing missile fuel and drone components in the area around the Ukrainian capital, the ministry said.
Russia launched missiles and 123 drones, 73 of them jet-powered drones, at Ukraine overnight, the Ukrainian air force said. Hits were recorded at 17 locations, it said.
U.S. Starlink problems return, Zelenskyy says
Ukraine is experiencing another slowdown in the U.S. Starshield system — SpaceX's military-grade version of the Starlink satellite internet service — that the country needs to defend itself against Russian attacks, Zelenskyy said Thursday on social media.
Military units have recorded "significant disruptions," including speed restrictions limiting Ukrainian drones to 161 kph (100 mph), Zelenskyy said, adding that a military investigation established that the restrictions weren't random errors.
Ukraine uses Starlink and Starshield for intercepting Russian drones and launching its own strikes.
Last month, limits on Ukrainian drone speeds severely disrupted operations and alarmed Kyiv officials who fear U.S. support could drop off.
Elon Musk acknowledged that his company SpaceX had throttled the Starlink internet service in Ukraine for about a week, saying the system couldn't be used for offensive strikes against Russia.
Zelenskyy said in Dublin that the speed limits cover operations in Russian-occupied parts of Ukraine and that Kyiv is trying to find out from U.S. officials what is going on. "If someone in America is making decisions that basically treat Ukrainian territory as if it is not Ukrainian, then this tells us where things are going," he said.
Russian colonel reportedly killed by a car bomb
A Russian serviceman was killed in St. Petersburg early Thursday when his vehicle exploded, according to Russia's Investigative Committee, the country's main criminal investigation agency. It didn't identify the victim or say who was behind the bombing.
The Fontanka news outlet said the victim was a colonel and that a bomb in his car exploded as he drove off.
Several senior Russian military officers have been killed by bombings and other attacks that Moscow blames on Ukraine. Kyiv has claimed responsibility for some attacks on Russian soil.

Two Iranian men have been found guilty of spying on journalists and a lawyer in conduct that was likely to assist Iran’s intelligence service.
Mostafa Sepahvand, 41, carried out surveillance and reconnaissance between August 2024 and March last year in a bid to inflict violence on “subjects” in the UK.

- The claim that the U.S. Air Force had held Maj. Jason Watson, an active-duty airman who publicly called for the impeachment of President Donald Trump, in solitary confinement for more than 80 days by November while he awaited court-martial is still under investigation.
- CNN reported that the Air Force took Watson into pretrial confinement on Aug. 18, under conditions his lawyer Christopher Mutimer later described as "basically in solitary confinement." Mutimer said in early October that Watson was "still in solitary confinement."
- Speaking to Snopes on Nov. 10, Mutimer confirmed Watson had been held in Calvert County Detention Center, Maryland, since Aug. 18, for a total of 85 days and counting. Mutimer explained that because Watson was a military officer, he could not be held with civilian prisoners, meaning he was "in a room by himself 22 to 23 hours a day." - A spokesperson for the Department of the Air Force told Snopes via email on Nov. 13 that Watson, "is held in administrative protective segregation — not punitive solitary confinement." The spokesperson said that Watson had "regular access to standard institutional amenities and programs."
In November, a claim (archived) circulated online that the U.S. Air Force had held Maj. Jason Watson, an active-duty airman who publicly called for the impeachment of President Donald Trump, in solitary confinement for more than 80 days while he awaited court-martial.
CNN reported that the Air Force ordered Watson into "pre-trial confinement" on Aug. 18. Two days later, on Aug. 20, Watson's lawyer Christopher Mutimer told CNN that Watson was "basically in solitary confinement." He repeated this claim in early October, telling CNN (at 1:46, archived) that Watson was "still in solitary confinement."
One X user who claimed Watson remained in solitary confinement in early November — 84 days after the Air Force first ordered him into pretrial confinement — wrote:
Maj. Jason Watson has been in 24-hour solitary confinement for 80+ days & has reportedly lost 20 pounds, all before any trial. UN experts consider solitary beyond 15 days to be torture. He offered to resign, give up all his benefits, & the Air Force said no. Because he protested.
The claim also circulated on Facebook and Threads (archived, archived). Snopes readers contacted us about the claim.
Speaking to Snopes on Nov. 10, Mutimer confirmed Watson had been detained at Maryland's Calvert County Detention Center since Aug. 18 and described conditions that he said met generally understood definitions for solitary confinement.
Mutimer said Watson "is in a room by himself 22 to 23 hours a day. No one stays in there with him, he is not allowed to have any interaction. When he's let out it's to shower, make a phone call, get some time in the yard by himself." He described Watson's cell as a "pen" where "the light is on all the time."
Mutimer added, "Because he's an officer, he is in the military, that contract says he is not allowed to be with anybody who is not in the military."
A spokesperson for the Department of the Air Force said in a statement on Nov. 13:
The Department of the Air Force can confirm that Maj Watson is not being held in solitary confinement. Maj Watson is held in administrative protective segregation—not punitive solitary confinement—at the Calvert County Detention Center (CCDC) pursuant to an official Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) between CCDC and the 11th Wing Security Forces Squadron (11 SFS) at Joint Base Anacostia-Bolling (JBAB).
Maj Watson is physically separated from CCDC's civilian general inmate population to comply with military policy and statutory segregation mandates. While separated from civilian detainees, Maj Watson does have regular access to standard institutional amenities and programs, including the facility library, religious services/chapel, and physical fitness time. He also retains normal access to defense counsel, military leadership visits, medical care, and personal visitation.
Because of the opposing descriptions of Watson's confinement from his lawyer and the Air Force, we leave this claim unrated. we leave this claim unrated.
By November, the docket of the Air Force's military justice branch showed Watson was due for general court-martial in February. Mutimer said he would argue a petition for Watson's pretrial release on Nov. 17.
Mutimer also confirmed the claim some social media users made that Watson had attempted to resign after his July 1 arrest but said officials had denied his resignation and instead pressed ahead with the court-martial, a move that Mutimer described as "absolutely unheard of."
Tracking Watson's case
Capitol Police arrested Watson on July 1 on after he publicly called for Trump's impeachment while wearing his Air Force uniform. A live stream (at 50:56) of the arrest showed Watson standing on the Capitol steps in uniform while holding a sign that read "Impeach Convict Remove."
Watson said at a news conference earlier that day that he was calling for Trump to be impeached because he thought the president and Vice President JD Vance had governed in an unconstitutional way throughout their administration.
Watson highlighted the war in Iran, Elon Musk's sweeping cuts to federal government and the Department of Homeland Security's immigration crackdown and killings of protesters as "high crimes and misdemeanors" (at 28:28) for which "the president and vice president must be impeached, convicted, and removed."
The Air Force major repeated his call for Trump and Vance's removal while speaking to CNN's Erin Burnett (at 1:52) on Aug. 17. Burnett said (at 2:41) during the interview that the military had placed a "gag order" on Watson after his July 1 protest and that he was "under investigation."
According to a later CNN report, the Air Force took Watson into pretrial confinement days after he spoke to the network.
CNN reported that the Air Force charged Watson with 10 violations of three articles of the Uniform Code of Military Justice, the military's legal framework, on Aug. 20. Mutimer reportedly spoke to Watson on that date and reported that he was "basically in solitary confinement."
On Sept. 29, The New York Times reported that an Air Force investigating officer had recommended Watson's case for general court-martial, the military's highest level of trial court.
According to the Judge Advocate General's Corps Department of the Air Force, which investigated and charged Watson, the major faced charges of four violations of articles 88, 92 and 133 of the UCMJ.
Article 88 (Page 34) of the UCMJ states that any commissioned officer who uses "contemptuous words" against certain public officials, which includes the president and vice president, should face a court-martial. Article 92 (Page 35) states that a person subject to the code that fails to obey an order or regulation can be subject to court-martial. Article 133 (Page 48) states that "Any commissioned officer, cadet, or midshipman who is convicted of conduct unbecoming an officer and a gentleman shall be punished as a court-martial may direct."
The code does not explicitly define what "conduct unbecoming an officer" means.
An Air Force spokesperson reportedly told Military.com in October that the Air Force had acted in accordance with the Rule for Court-Martial 305 when it took Watson into pretrial confinement in August. That rule says someone can be placed in pretrial confinement if there is probable cause they committed "an offense triable by court-martial."
That rule also says that someone taken into pretrial confinement can ask a military judge to review the "propriety" of the confinement, meaning whether it is appropriate. Mutimer said such a review for Watson would happen on Nov. 17.
According to the UCMJ's Article 13 (Page 5), it is prohibited to punish a service member awaiting trial. Any confinement before trial must not "be any more rigorous than the circumstances require to insure his presence, but he may be subjected to minor punishment during that period for infractions of discipline."
At the time of this writing, Watson had not been convicted or sentenced. Punishments for service members convicted by court-martial range from reprimands and salary reductions to dismissal or discharge.

Cake, according to a group of retired scientists, has become the most visible product of the Sher-e-Kashmir University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology of Kashmir (SKUAST-K).
The S&T Retired Forum says cake-cutting ceremonies have become almost a daily feature at the university, making its administration a “strong contender” for holding the highest number of such events.
The forum’s president, Dr. G.A. Wani, raised the issue in an open letter to the lieutenant governor, chief minister and agriculture minister.
The letter comes as the vice-chancellor’s extended tenure approaches its end and the university prepares to appoint a successor.
The retired scientists say their concerns are about the institution, not any individual. They want the government to judge SKUAST-K by the quality of its teaching, research and graduates rather than public celebrations and rankings.
One of their main concerns is whether the university has enough teachers to handle its growing student population.
Enrollment has increased from around 2,100 to more than 6,000, while the university has roughly 400 teachers.
The forum estimates that the student-teacher ratio may have worsened from 1:5 to 1:15.
It also points to classes with more than 100 students, raising concerns about the quality of practical training and the attention students receive from teachers.
The forum questions the university’s emphasis on improved rankings and argues that its academic performance should be judged through more concrete results.
These include the number of graduates qualifying in Agricultural Scientists Recruitment Board (ASRB) examinations, PhD scholars securing research positions at ICAR institutes and other institutions, and technologies developed by the university that have helped farmers.
According to figures cited by the forum, only three SKUAST-K PhD graduates appeared in the ASRB selection process over five years, and two qualified as scientists.
The forum says these figures, if verified, raise questions about doctoral supervision, laboratory facilities and the overall standard of research.
It also points to the hundreds of agriculture PhD holders reportedly looking for jobs in Jammu and Kashmir.
Against this backdrop, it questions the continued extensions and reappointments of retired employees.
The letter also seeks details of the role, responsibilities and contribution of a retired director who continues to be associated with the university.
Recruitment is another major concern, as the forum refers to an allegation that more than 50 people appointed during the current administration come from Tral, the hometown of the incumbent vice-chancellor.
It makes clear that the claim has not been supported by documentary evidence. However, the forum says such allegations can damage public trust and calls on the university to publish selection criteria, merit lists and recruitment figures broken down by region and category.
The retired scientists have also questioned the recent selection of university directors. They allege that experienced and reputed scientists were overlooked in favour of candidates whose qualifications and experience raise questions.
They want an independent review of the selection process, including the criteria used, candidate assessments and marks awarded.
The university administration had not officially responded to the forum’s letter. When Kashmir Observer sought its comments, some officials declined to speak, while others said they were not authorised to address the media. A few indicated that the university might issue a statement on the proposed independent inquiry. No official response was available at the time of publication.
Meanwhile, the forum has welcomed the new facilities inaugurated by the lieutenant governor but questioned the publicity surrounding these events. It wonders whether the celebrations could amount to indirect campaigning, particularly at a time when the vice-chancellor’s post has been advertised.
To address its concerns, the forum has proposed an independent panel of agricultural scientists, academicians and outside experts to examine the university’s functioning.
“The panel would review faculty strength, teaching standards, research output, patents, the impact of research on farmers, examination results, placements, recruitment, director appointments and the use of public funds,” the letter notes.
The forum wants the findings made public, while keeping confidential service records protected.
Its seven demands include an independent audit before the appointment of the next vice-chancellor, merit-based recruitment and appointments, a review of extensions granted to retired staff and the selection of directors, better faculty strength and laboratory facilities, and a time-bound plan to support young scientists.
“The university belongs to the people of Jammu & Kashmir,” the letter says.
The retired scientists conclude with a pointed question about the university’s legacy: will SKUAST-K be remembered for the scientists it produced or the cakes it cut?

Consumer tech focussed venture capital firm Fireside Ventures has seen a second exit from its leadership and investment team in two weeks. Prayag Mohanty, principal at Fireside Ventures, who led its early-stage bets, has quit the firm, Inc42 has learnt from multiple sources. His exit follows a bigger leadership change at Fireside Ventures. Earlier this month, the firm said that cofounder and partner Vinay Singh has stepped down after nearly a decade at the firm. Responding to Inc42's query, Fireside Ventures confirmed Mohanty’s exit. "Prayag Mohanty is moving on from his role of Principal at Fireside Ventures. We value his contributions made during his time with us, and wish him the best in his future endeavours," Fireside said in a statement to Inc42. Another Blow For Fireside Mohanty joined Fireside Ventures as a Principal in January 2020. He was one of five principals listed on the firm's investment team, alongside Ankur Khaitan, Shuchi Pandya, Varun Varma and Ankita Balotia. As a principal leading Fireside’s early stage investments, Mohanty fronted several of the firm's seed stage bets over the past year, including a ₹8 Cr round in Gurugram-based men's personal care brand Unbound, a ₹20 Cr round in Noida-based Oroos Confectionery and another ₹8 Cr seed round in kids wellness startup Wellopia. In earlier media reports, he was quoted as saying that Fireside Ventures is ramping up investments in pre-product-market-fit and even pre-revenue startups through a co-investment model with other funds and angel investors, with 8-10 such deals in the pipeline from the new third fund. Before Fireside, Mohanty had spent about seven years as a principal at IvyCap Ventures from 2013 to 2020, and was involved in deals for listed jewellery giant BlueStone, BiryaniByKilo and Vinculum. The key departures come less than a year after Fireside announced the final close of its Fund IV at ₹2,265 Cr (about $253 Mn) in December 2025. With Singh’s exit, the firm is being led by founder and managing partner Kanwaljit Singh and cofounders and partners Kannan Sitaram and Dipanjan Basu. The fund drew commitments from LPs including the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority (ADIA), Investment Corporation of Dubai, HarbourVest, Waterfield and Fidelity International. With Fund IV, Fireside's assets under management across four funds stand at ₹5,300 Cr (about $650 Mn).

In the Israeli legislative elections held in late October 2026, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud party and its allies secured 53 seats in the 120-member Knesset, falling short of the 61-seat majority required to govern. The Yashar party, led by Gadi Eisenkot, alongside other opposition factions, won 48 seats. Notably, Arab-led parties made historic gains, winning 19 seats and becoming potential “kingmakers”. Following the vote, President Isaac Herzog formally accepted the results. He opened a two-day consultation window with party leaders to determine who is best positioned to assemble a stable coalition.
In this context, a video is being shared on social media (here, here, and here) with the claim that it shows the Palestinian flag being hoisted in the Israeli Parliament. Let’s verify the claim made in the post in this article.
Claim: The video shows the Palestinian flag being hoisted in the Israeli Parliament building.
Fact: The video does not show the Palestinian flag being hoisted in the Israeli Parliament. It shows a pro-Palestine activist replacing the German national flag with a Palestinian flag on a flagpole outside the Reichstag building, which houses the German Parliament (Bundestag), in Berlin on 08 November 2026. Hence, the claim made in the post is FALSE.
A reverse image search of keyframes from the viral video led us to multiple media reports (here, here, and here) featuring visuals similar to those seen in the viral video. According to these reports, the incident took place outside the Reichstag building, which houses the German Parliament (Bundestag), in Berlin on Sunday, 08 November 2026.
The reports (here, here) state that a 22-year-old pro-Palestine activist climbed a 30-metre-high flagpole in front of the Reichstag building at around 11:30 am, removed the German national flag, and replaced it with a Palestinian flag.
The group ‘Peacefully Against Genocide‘ claimed responsibility for the incident, stating that the action was a protest against the German government’s pro-Israel policy and its silence on alleged human rights violations in Gaza.
According to a press release issued by Berlin Police on 08 November 2026, two people who allegedly assisted the 22-year-old activist were detained and later released after their identities were established. The Palestinian flag was subsequently removed with the assistance of the Berlin Fire Brigade. Police also launched an investigation into suspected offences, including insulting state symbols, damaging government property, trespassing, and violating Berlin’s assembly law.
To sum up, the viral video shows the Palestinian flag hoisted outside the German Parliament, not the Israeli Parliament.

A widespread outage at Microsoft brought Outlook, Teams and several other Microsoft 365 applications to a standstill for thousands of users globally on Thursday. Users faced disruption accessing emails, work files and productivity tools for over 10 hours during the outage. The disruption also spilled over to third-party platforms, with OpenAI and Anthropic reporting issues with their Microsoft 365 connectors. As per outage reports on Downdetector, outages in India peaked at 2,162 around 11:44 PM on Thursday (November 12. Reports climbed again to 2,254 around 8:59 AM. Globally, Downdetector recorded more than 38,000 reports of Microsoft 365 problems and around 4,500 reports related to Microsoft Teams at around 2:07 PM ET on Thursday. Microsoft initially attributed the disruption to elevated load across its infrastructure in multiple regions. Later, it clarified that the issue was not driven by an increase in traffic but by several servers becoming unexpectedly unavailable, placing additional pressure on the remaining infrastructure. In an update on X, the company said it had paused all deployments, redirected additional traffic away from the affected infrastructure and begun restoring services. "We determined the elevated load isn't driven by an increase in traffic, but by a number of servers being unexpectedly unavailable; straining the remaining infrastructure. We're working to safely return them to service," Microsoft said. Microsoft has been issuing regular updates on X about its efforts to restore services. The company initially said it was testing a configuration change to address a problem that was causing servers to fail automated health checks and become unavailable. However, the recovery efforts did not provide the expected relief. Microsoft subsequently found that a core process on affected servers was becoming overwhelmed, resulting in capacity loss. It also found that some of the servers that returned to service became unresponsive again upon receiving traffic. To address the issue, Microsoft began redirecting traffic through alternative routes, temporarily restricting certain types of traffic and adjusting network protocols. It also introduced strategic traffic-blocking measures to improve server stability. In a subsequent update, the company said these measures had resulted in partial recovery across some regions but had not delivered sustained service restoration. Microsoft said it was exploring alternative approaches to address persistent traffic management imbalances and improve infrastructure stability. In its latest update on X, posted today, Microsoft said it was pursuing multiple workstreams to reduce the impact of the outage. “We're engaged in multiple workstreams to alleviate impact, address our current blocker, and returning portions of service infrastructure back to a healthy state. A more comprehensive update can be found at MO1550821 in the Microsoft 365 admin center, as well as http://status.cloud.microsoft if the admin center is not available to you,” the company posted. What Services Were Affected? The disruption primarily affected services dependent on Exchange Online, Microsoft's cloud-based email and messaging platform. Outlook users faced difficulties accessing their mailboxes through web, desktop and mobile applications. Email delivery was also delayed, while some users reported connectivity issues. The disruption extended to Microsoft 365 applications, with users experiencing difficulties accessing recently used files. Some pages in the Microsoft 365 admin centre also failed to load. Microsoft Copilot was among the affected services. Users reported problems loading Copilot Chat and receiving responses through web and desktop applications. Its ability to retrieve work-related information, including emails, calendars and files, was also disrupted. Microsoft Teams continued to support core messaging and online meetings largely normally. However, features dependent on Exchange Online, including calendars and meeting scheduling, were affected. Some users also reported difficulties creating chats in organisations using Information Barriers. Other affected services included Microsoft Planner, Microsoft To Do, Microsoft Defender, Microsoft Purview, Microsoft Graph, Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, SharePoint Online, Universal Print and Windows 365. The outage extended beyond Microsoft's own applications, affecting third-party services that depend on its infrastructure. OpenAI said it was investigating an issue with its Microsoft connectors that could prevent new connections from being established and cause certain tools to malfunction. Anthropic also reported an issue with an upstream provider affecting its Microsoft 365 connector. The disruption highlighted how outages in widely used cloud infrastructure can have a cascading impact on businesses and services that rely on third-party integrations. The outage also affected businesses and government organisations that depend on Microsoft's tech suite. Microsoft earlier reported an outage affecting its Azure cloud platform in October 2026, which disrupted its productivity software suite and affected businesses across several industries. The latest update indicates that the recovery process is still ongoing, with the company yet to confirm a complete restoration of affected services.

Gadi Eisenkot sharply criticized Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu days after the Israeli leader attacked Arab lawmakers in a divisive speech.
Gadi Eisenkot, the former military chief who is trying to form the next Israeli government, accused Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Friday of fueling a “racist” campaign against the country’s Arab citizens, in some of the strongest public criticism of his rival’s attacks on the community.

“The attempt to marginalize them and vilify them collectively is a profound violation of the principles of statesmanship,” Mr. Eisenkot said. “It dishonors Israel’s Declaration of Independence and the values we take pride in as a Jewish and democratic state.”
The Declaration of Independence says all citizens have equal social and political rights “irrespective of religion, race or sex.”

India getting bowled out for 89 against New Zealand in the fourth ODI here has left head coach Gautam Gambhir concerned as the collapse is not one off and happened in conditions that are similar to what the team will encounter during next year's World Cup in South Africa.
After India suffered a crushing 244-run loss to New Zealand here on Friday, Gambhir admitted that the manner and speed of the batting collapse, rather than the low total, was a worry ahead of the global event.
"You're always concerned when you get bundled out for 90-odd. Why won't I be concerned? These are conditions which are going to be closest to what we might get during the World Cup," Gambhir said at the post-match press conference.
"The bigger concern is not the runs. It's how quickly we got bundled out, around 26 or 27 overs. That is something which is always a concern," he added.
India had also struggled in the previous match, slipping to 111 for seven while chasing 135 in a rain-curtailed match, prompting Gambhir to underline the need for both technical and mental preparedness against the moving ball.
He said the first 10 overs in New Zealand are particularly challenging, unlike in India where the initial phase is generally the easiest period for batting.
"If you get 35 or 40 in the first 10 overs without losing a wicket, that is also good enough. Here, it's probably the most difficult time," he said.
Gambhir also said that India needed to be more decisive against the lengths employed by New Zealand pacers Matt Henry and Kyle Jamieson, particularly the deliveries that left batters caught in two minds between going forward and playing off the back foot.
"I thought, more than the wobble seam, it's the areas that have probably created problems for us. It was that length where you couldn't go forward, you couldn't go back. It was that half-half length," he said.
Praising Henry's approach, Gambhir said the New Zealand pacer consistently attacked the stumps and challenged both edges of the bat, something the Indian bowling unit could learn from.
"He got Rohit in the slips and then got Virat and Shreyas beaten on the inside edge. That is something we need to learn, how consistently we can hit the stumps and keep hitting those pads as well," he said.
Gambhir also acknowledged that dropped catches proved costly, particularly the opportunities given to New Zealand centurion Will Young, who went on to make 125.
"He got those two chances and made the most of it. Things could have been a lot different, but there's always hindsight to what you do. We dropped catches, no one else did. So we had to pay for it," he said.
Defending the inexperienced Indian pace attack, Gambhir said the team had plenty to learn from playing in unfamiliar conditions but backed the young bowlers.
"I feel proud of everyone. Good days will pass, bad days will pass as well. There will be days like this, because this is what you learn from. Because the amount of inexperience you have in bowling attacks, it can be difficult as a captain and as a support staff as well. Because you're actually learning on the job.
"It's not like you've come into international cricket with no experience at all. So when you have so much inexperience, and when you come into alien conditions, but the way you've played in this one-day series, I think not only me, I think all of us should be proud of that.
He also explained the decision to play a wrist-spinner instead of Mohammed Siraj, saying the team felt a tweaker would be more useful on the bigger ground and provide an attacking option in the middle overs.
On the batting combination, Gambhir said India were trying to maintain continuity while giving players opportunities in different positions, adding that Ruturaj Gaikwad was preferred at the top because of his greater experience as an opener compared to Ishan Kishan.
Despite the heavy defeat, Gambhir backed the team to recover in the series decider, saying the players had enough experience and quality to bounce back.
"I'm sure the guys will turn up. It's important that they're hurting. I always believe that people should be hurting in the dressing room when you have this kind of a performance. If you're hurting, then obviously we can come back really strong," he said.

Disney's 3D movies shine on Meta's Quest 3, it's just a shame it took so long
Finally, you can watch Avatar in 3D HFR at home.
3D movies have been, and continue to be, a bit of a gimmick. But the technology can also be used well — just take a look at James Cameron's Avatar films, or CG movies like Moana and Zootopia. With the death of 3D TVs, though, there haven't been many easy ways for consumers to see 3D content at home. Enter the VR headset: For years, intrepid VR owners have been ripping 3D Blu-rays to enjoy on their stereoscopic displays. Apple made 3D films a key selling point for the Vision Pro. And now Meta has finally jumped into the game with its own library of 3D films for Quest 3 and 3S headsets, which launched alongside a new Disney+ app featuring 3D content and environments. Finally, you can enjoy Tron: Legacy as it was truly meant to be seen (sort of).
As someone who's spent dozens of hours watching 3D movies on the Apple Vision Pro, I was keen to see how Meta delivered them on significantly cheaper headsets. My big takeaway? 3D movies are an exciting new feature for existing Quest 3 and Quest 3S owners, but they're also constrained by the company's OS. It's also unclear why it took so long to make 3D movies happen on Quest headsets, or why the popular Quest 2 is left out entirely.
First, the good: Disney has made its library of 3D films available on Disney+ (actual titles depend on your region), including the entire run of Marvel, Pixar and recent Star Wars titles. Disney+ subscribers just need to select a title, confirm it has 3D support and hit play. The opening scenes of Guardians of the Galaxy and the car chase from Black Panther all looked great on the Quest 3, with a wonderful sense of depth that you don't get from watching them on 2D screens. Disney+ also includes the high framerate 3D versions of the Avatar films, which look incredible on the Quest 3, and were previously only available to watch at home on the Apple Vision Pro.
I've long thought 3D movies looked better on VR headsets than theaters, since they're far brighter than a projected cinema screen dimmed by 3D glasses, and that remains true for the Quest 3. If you still have a Quest 3 or 3S collecting dust, and you're already a Disney+ subscriber, it's worth checking out the 3D library of movies. Just be sure to throw on a pair of headphones, as the Quest's tinny speakers have very little depth and no low-end impact. The Quest 3 supports both Dolby Vision and Dolby Atmos, but those are basically marketing terms on this device. The headset's LCD screens don't support true HDR of any kind, and Atmos doesn't make much of a difference on its weak speakers.
Meta has updated its Horizon OS to more resemble Apple's visionOS over the years, but unfortunately, it's not nearly as flexible when it comes to playing video. You can't just rescale the Disney+ window on the fly to make it larger — it has to fit into a specific spot in Meta's OS. As a front row cinema sicko, I prefer having video windows completely filling my field of view, and occasionally bleeding into my peripheral vision. The only way to achieve that on the Quest 3 is by playing 3D videos within the cinema environment, where you can choose to sit in the front, middle or back rows. It gets the job done, but it's not ideal if you want to juggle a 3D video along with other VR apps.
While it's nice to see Meta finally offering 3D movies, I genuinely wonder why it took the company so long to do so. The Quest 3 launched in the fall of 2023! There's nothing technically preventing the Quest 2 or 1 from streaming 3D either. I figure that Apple has maintained some sort of exclusivity over 3D Disney+ content since the Vision Pro launched in 2024, but that didn't prevent Meta from offering 3D films on its own. At this point, as Quest sales are on the extreme decline, it's not really much of a selling point.
Perhaps Meta just wanted to have a shiny new feature for its upcoming $1,300 VR Glasses, which is set to arrive in spring 2027. I haven't tested those yet, but I can imagine watching high quality 3D movies on a much lighter pair of glasses will be much more comfortable than strapping a Quest headset on your noggin. For now, though, it's certainly a nice feature to have if you still own a Quest 3 or 3S.

Ujjain (Madhya Pradesh): The Chandesari Junction on the 177-km highway stretch, constructed by the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) at a cost of about Rs 3,451 crore, has become a major concern for motorists. Even two years after its construction, the underpass near the junction remains non-functional, forcing thousands of villagers to cross the busy highway amid fast-moving heavy vehicles, posing a serious risk of accidents
The NHAI has constructed these highway stretches on the Dewas Road under four separate packages. The first package, covering 41.42 km between Dewas and Ujjain, was built at a cost of Rs 842.52 crore. The second package, part of the Ujjain-Garoth section, spans 42.15 km and costs Rs 909.84 crore. The third package covers 47.80 km at a cost of Rs 876.37 crore, while the fourth package spans 46.15 km and was constructed for Rs 823.05 crore.
These ambitious projects were undertaken with a view to managing vehicular traffic arriving from Delhi, Rajasthan, Gujarat and Maharashtra during the 'Simhastha Mahaparv'-2028. Due to damage in certain sections of the Ujjain-Garoth route, full-scale traffic operations have not yet commenced on that stretch. Nevertheless, vehicular movement continues unabated along several routes via Ujjain-Chandesari Junction toward Dewas and Indore; from Chandesari Junction via Tapobhumi toward Badnawar and from Chandesari through Ujjain toward the Agar-Shajapur road.
The NHAI had constructed underpasses on both sides of the Badnawar-Tapobhumi-Dewas-Indore road flyover at the Chandesari Junction; however, these have remained non-functional for the past two to three years. They are barely noticeable unless one looks very closely. Villagers explained that both underpasses were built well below ground level, causing them to become waterlogged. Initially, local villagers took the risk of crossing at the Chandesari Junction and brought the issue to the attention of public representatives and concerned officials.
Later, the villagers themselves broke through a wall at the Chandesari Junction to create a passage. The current situation is such that large vehicles frequently pass through from all directions, while villagers also constantly cross the junction. Several drivers noted that unless one exercises extreme caution while driving, an accident is almost inevitable. Inquiries at the Nagjhiri police station revealed an increase in accidents in the area.
When contacted, Shivam Sharma, the NHAI's Ujjain project in-charge, acknowledged that both underpasses at the Chandesari Junction are not operational. He stated that a new proposal will be drafted to construct 500-metre service roads on both sides of the Chandesari Junction, which will spare villagers from having to travel long distances. Regarding the flaws in the original project, he mentioned that he could not comment, as he had been posted to the position only five months ago.

Over six months after Rishi Gupta stepped down from his role as CEO of Fino Payments Bank, the fintech company is now set to get a new managing director (MD) and CEO. Today, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) approved the appointment of ICICI Bank veteran Pratap Singh as its new MD and CEO for 3 years. Singh is set to take charge by November 27. "The board of directors of the bank shall take necessary steps for his appointment, which will be subject to approval of shareholders of the bank. The bank will be intimate to the stock exchanges when Pratap Singh formally takes charge as the MD & CEO of the bank," Fino said. The new CEO brings over 29 years of experience across the banking sector in India and the UK. He has held leadership positions at ICICI Bank India, ICICI Bank UK and SBI UK. At ICICI Bank UK, he served as head of retail and SME banking for the UK and Europe, and has expertise spanning retail and SME banking, liabilities, digital transformation and branch-led profitability. The leadership change follows a turbulent year for Fino. Gupta, the company’s former CEO was arrested in February 2026 in connection with an investigation into alleged GST evasion of over ₹840 Cr linked to online betting platforms. Subsequently, Gupta requested for a voluntary early retirement, beginning May 21. Since then, the bank’s CFO, Ketan Merchant, took charge as interim CEO in May and has held the position since. Fino’s head of finance, investor relations and analytics Anup Aggarwal stepped up to fill in the interim CFO role. The leadership transition also comes at a time when Fino is bidding to convert to a small finance bank (SFB). Since receiving an 'in-principle' from the RBI to convert to an SFB back in December 2025. However, it must be noted that the RBI has given an 18-month window to complete the transition and meet the net-worth requirement of ₹300 Cr. Despite recent regulatory scrutiny and an investigation involving its CEO, the bank stated it remains on track to finish the process within the stipulated timeline. Amid all this, Fino’s financial and stock performance has taken a considerable hit. On the financial front, Fino reported a net loss of ₹20.9 Cr in Q2 FY27, against a net profit of ₹15.4 Cr in the year-ago quarter, marking its second consecutive quarterly loss. At the same time, its total income declined 16.6% YoY to ₹333.6 Cr. Operationally, Fino reported mixed business performance for the month of October 2026. The company's transaction throughput declined 18% YoY to ₹3,541 Cr, while the number of deposit accounts opened fell 19% to 2.3 Lakh. Average total deposits rose 9% to ₹2,886 Cr, while digitally active customers increased 12% to 65.1 Lakh. CMS throughput grew 12% to ₹7,514 Cr. Loan referral disbursals surged 316% to ₹301 Cr. However, the bank's total deposits crossed ₹3,000 Cr for the first time, peaking at ₹3,044 Cr during the month. The company’s shares have plunged close to 50% on a year to date (YTD) basis. Fino's shares closed today's trading session 2% higher at 129.95 apiece on the BSE.

Pakistan’s former Prime Minister Imran Khan was taken to hospital in Islamabad late on Tuesday (November 10, 2026) for medical treatment and returned to prison, sources said.
Khan, who is imprisoned in Adiala Jail in Rawalpindi, had an eye check-up at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS), one of the officials said on Wednesday (November 11).
“He had some blood pressure issues ... and was given required treatment last night. He has been shifted back to his prison cell,” the person said.
The cricketer-turned-politician has faced multiple corruption charges since he lost power in a no-confidence vote in 2022, and has been in prison for more than three years. All of Khan’s convictions bar one have been suspended or overturned, with appeals pending. He denies wrongdoing and says the charges are politically motivated, a claim the government denies.
Khan’s lawyers say the 74-year-old’s health has deteriorated in prison and that he has lost significant vision in his right eye.
It is the first known instance of Khan being taken to hospital for treatment and returned to jail since August, when his hospital visit was cut short.
A Pakistani court has also ordered jail authorities to allow Khan’s legal team to see him and his wife, his party said.
His party’s deputy chairman, Shah Mehmood Qureshi, was also taken to hospital in the eastern city of Lahore from a jail in the same city on Tuesday (November 10). He remains in hospital.

UP man murders ‘online game partner’ in Bengal after argument escalates, arrested in Delhi
Twenty-six-year-old Anjali Sau was found dead at her relative's place on Tuesday in Bengal's North 24 Parganas.
A 30-year-old man was arrested from Delhi’s Anand Vihar area on Friday by the West Bengal police in connection with the murder of a 26-year-old woman in Baranagar in North 24 Parganas.
The body of Anjali Sau, 26, was found at a relative’s house on Tuesday. A post mortem examination revealed that she was assaulted before the murder, though there were no signs of sexual assault, police said.
Police suspect dispute over ‘relationship’, money
The accused has been identified as Dharamveer Kumar, a resident of Uttar Pradesh, and the two were online gaming partners. Kumar allegedly killed Sau on Tuesday after an argument broke out between the two over their relationship, according to the police. A money dispute is also suspected and an investigation in the case is still underway.
“They were online game partners and were close to each other. Kumar strangulated her to death after an argument broke out over their relationship. She was physically assaulted. We have not found any signs of sexual assault,” a senior officer of Barrackpore police said.
Kumar allegedly arrived in Bengal on Sunday and stayed at a lodge in Dakshineshwar. He visited Sau who was staying at a relative’s place in Baranagar. The two reportedly had tea together before an argument broke out, which escalated and Kumar strangulated Sau with her dupatta.
Accused stole victim's phone, texted her parents
Kumar fled the spot and stayed at his lodge for a few hours in Dakshineshwar before boarding a train to Delhi from Howrah station. He also stole Sau’s mobile phone and sent around eight “arbitrary messages” to her parents and also made a WhatsApp call, which lasted a few seconds, police said.
“He will be brought back to Kolkata from Delhi on transit remand. Once we question him, we will get more details why he made those calls and sent those messages. Preliminary questioning revealed that he murdered the victim out of revenge over some rejection in their relationship,” said the officer.
Police said an investigation in the murder case has been started on the basis of the complaint of the victim’s parents.

Snopes found not 20, but 25 bills related to the regulation of firearms had been prefiled for 2027 legislative session as of this writing. Of the state representatives and senators who'd introduced the bills, 11 were Democrats and three were Republicans. Of those bills, 20 were introduced in the House and five of them in the Senate.
Soon after Democrats swept the Texas House of Representatives in November's midterm election, a rumor spread that they had already filed approximately 20 bills related to gun control.
The claim circulated on social media, including on YouTube, Instagram and Facebook. Meanwhile, on X, posts like the one below enumerated the 20 supposed bills, alleging that "Texas Democrats are filing a FLOOD of proposed bills that would TAKE AWAY gun rights for Americans" (archived):
Snopes readers searched the website seeking to confirm the veracity of the claim.
The claim was true, though Snopes found not 20, but 25 bills related to the regulation of firearms had been prefiled for the 2027 legislative session as of this writing.
Of those bills, 20 were House bills and five were Senate bills.
Of the state representatives and senators who'd introduced the bills, 11 were Democrats and three were Republicans.
List of prefiled bills related to gun control in the Texas legislature
On Nov. 9, prefiling began at the Texas legislature — a period when the state's lawmakers can begin to file bills for consideration for the upcoming session. Sitting lawmakers reportedly filed "more than 1,000 bills" before midday that day.
(It's worth noting that while Democrats won the majority of the Texas House, Republicans kept theirs in the state Senate. Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa is a Democrat. She is set to replace Republican Greg Abbott.)
Among the bills Snopes identified, five would prohibit the transfer or sale of semiautomatic firearms to people younger than 21. Two of them would increase the criminal penalty for allowing children to access firearms.
The bills are as follows:
- HB 103 - Author: Rep. Mando Martinez (Democrat). This bill would make it possible to prosecute "the criminal offense of reckless discharge of a firearm" in larger swaths of the territory in Texas.
- HB 659 - Author: Rep. Joe Moody (Democrat). This bill would require "a licensed firearms dealer to report certain sales or transfers of multiple firearms or firearm magazines to law enforcement," creating a new criminal offense.
- SB 80 - Author: Sen. Judith Zaffirini (Democrat). This bill would ban "certain transfers, purchases, and possession of assault weapons," creating new criminal offenses.
- HB 613 - Author: Rep. Suleman Lalani (Democrat). This bill would require "a national instant criminal background check in connection with private firearm transfers" and create a new criminal offense.
- HB 712 - Author: Rep. Erin Gámez (Democrat). This bill would allow cities and counties "to regulate or prohibit the carrying of a firearm on the premises of certain libraries."
- SB 308 - Author: Sen. Roland Gutierrez, a Democrat (and others). This bill would ban the making and possession of 3D-printed "firearms and major components of firearms," but also "the distribution or publication" of the digital files that serve to print these firearms and their components. It would create new criminal offenses.
- HB 606 - Author: Lalani. This bill would ban "the transfer of firearms to or the purchase or possession of firearms by persons younger than 21 years of age." It would create a new criminal offense.
- HB 218 - Author: Rep. Ann Johnson (Democrat). This bill would allow members of a family or household and law enforcement officers to ask a court to curtail someone's ability to access firearms if they think the person poses an immediate danger due to mental illness. It would allow for the "creation, issuance, and enforcement" of "extreme risk protective orders."
- HB 618 - Author: Moody. This bill would ban the "transfer of firearm magazines to recipients who are prohibited from possessing the type of firearm for which the magazine is designed or made" and create a new criminal offense.
- HB 610 - Author: Lalani. This bill would ban "the transfer of firearms to certain recipients who are younger than 21 years of age."
- HB 660 -Author: Moody. This bill would require "certain persons prohibited by law from owning, possessing, or controlling a firearm" to give up the firearms they own, possess or control.
- HB 173 - Author: Moody. This bill would ban "the transfer of certain semiautomatic rifles" people younger than 21 and it would both create a criminal offense and increase a criminal penalty. It would also create some exceptions when a person younger than 21 may access such weapons.
- HB 857 - Author: Rep. Rafael Anchía (Democrat). Similarly to HB 173, this bill would ban "the transfer of certain semiautomatic rifles to certain recipients younger than 21 years of age," creating some exceptions.
- SB 327 - Author: Gutierrez (and others). Similarly to HB 173 and HB 857, the bill would ban "the transfer of certain semiautomatic rifles to certain recipients younger than 21 years of age."
- HB 806 - Author: Rep. Ron Reynolds (Democrat). Similarly to HB 173, HB 857 and SB 327, the bill would ban "the transfer of semiautomatic rifles to certain recipients" younger than 21 years old.
- HB 771 - Author: Pooja Sethi (Democrat). Similarly to HB 173, HB 857, SB 327 and HB 806, the bill would ban "the transfer of semiautomatic rifles to certain recipients" younger than 21 years old.
- HB 533 - Author: Rep. Carl Tepper (Republican ). This bill would ban "the carrying of concealed handguns by handgun license holders on the premises of certain polling places on the day of an election or while early voting is in progress."
- HB 658 - Author: Moody. This bill would make it possible to prosecute and punish "the offense of making a firearm accessible to a child" and it would increase a criminal penalty.
- HB 612 - Author: Lalani. This bill would ban "a sex offender from possessing a firearm."
- HB 576 - Author: Lalani. This bill would ban "sex offenders from purchasing firearms."
- SB 170 - Author: Sen. Brent Hagenbuch (Republican ). This bill would increase the criminal penalty for burglarizing a vehicle to steal a firearm.
- HB 773 - Author: Rep. A.J. Louderback (Republican). This bill would make it an aggravating factor to use or show a firearm during the commission of certain felony offenses, raising "the minimum term of imprisonment" and changing parole rules.
- SB 234 - Author: Sen. Carol Alvarado, a Democrat (and others).This would ban people convicted of "certain family violence misdemeanors" from owning a firearm.
- HB 609 - Author: Lalani. Similarly to HB 658, this bill would increase "the criminal penalty for the offense of making a firearm accessible to a child."
- HB 859 - Author: Anchía. This bill would increase "the criminal penalty" for "discharging a firearm in certain municipalities."

While this claim spread in 2026, the actual incident happened in 2020.
A claim is spreading online that a bald eagle attacked a $950 "government drone" in midair, sending it crashing into Lake Michigan.
Social media users shared the story on Facebook and Reddit, prompting Snopes readers to search the website to determine whether a bald eagle had, in fact, launched a successful attack against a foreign object in its airspace.
This story is true — although it happened years ago, not in 2026. It is also worth noting that while some posts online appear to show a bald eagle flying at a drone, there is no actual footage of the incident, according to the Michigan Department of Environment, Great Lakes, and Energy, or EGLE — the agency whose drone lost to the eagle.
Michigan state officials confirmed the eagle's assault in an Aug. 13, 2020, news release titled, "Shoreline-mapping EGLE drone sent to watery Lake Michigan grave by U.P. bald eagle." (U.P. is a reference to Michigan's Upper Peninsula.)
Here's how that release began:
An Upper Peninsula bald eagle launched an airborne attack on a drone operated by a Michigan Department of Environment, Great Lakes, and Energy (EGLE) pilot last month, tearing off a propeller and sending the aircraft to the bottom of Lake Michigan.
The brazen eagle vs. EGLE onslaught took place near Escanaba in Michigan's Upper Peninsula on July 21 when EGLE environmental quality analyst and drone pilot Hunter King was mapping shoreline erosion for use in the agency's efforts to document and help communities cope with high water levels.
King had completed about seven minutes of the mapping flight — his fourth of the day in the area — when satellite reception got spotty. He pressed the "Go Home" recall button. The drone dutifully turned, reacquiring a strong satellite feed.
King was watching his video screen as the drone beelined for home, but suddenly it began twirling furiously. "It was like a really bad rollercoaster ride," said King. When he looked up, the drone was gone, and an eagle was flying away. A nearby couple, whose pastimes include watching the local eagles attack seagulls and other birds, later confirmed they saw the eagle strike something but were surprised to learn it was a drone. Both King and the couple said the eagle appeared uninjured as it flew from the scene of the crime.
The release also confirmed that the drone was "a $950 Phantom 4 Pro Advanced" and shared data indicating that the eagle tore off a propeller, as many of the claim posts said (emphasis ours):
Data from the flight records detailed the drone's final moments:
- The eagle strike occurred 7:39.7 into the flight roughly four-tenths of a mile from King and 162 feet above the water
- Its speed instantly dropped from 22 mph to 10. Within a half-second the flight record shows the beginning of downward spiral along with "excessive spinning" warnings
- In the next 3.5 seconds the drone sent 27 warning notifications including one indicating a propeller had been torn off
- Gaining momentum as it fell, its last communication came at 34 feet above the water, falling at 30 feet per second, or 20.4 mph.
Per the release, King and the unidentified couple searched for the drone, "but hours of scouring the shoreline were fruitless." An unmanned aircraft systems coordinator with the state agency, Arthur Ostaszewski, also attempted to find the drone using a kayak, snorkeling gear and "telemetric data from the flight that pinpointed exactly where the drone hit the lake." He, too, was unsuccessful, even after walking a grid pattern for two hours — "like I was playing Battleship and wanted to cover the entire board," he said.
A week later, however, a team of Michigan state employees — which the agency cheekily dubbed in a news release as the Willful Eagle Trauma Team Engaged in Retrieval, or WETTER — managed to uncover the drone in almost the exact same location after "the previously murky water had cleared due to shifting winds and currents." EGLE shared a few pictures of the recovery effort on X, then known as Twitter:
The agency noted that the drone was not recording at the time of the bald eagle's assault, meaning that there would not be any footage of the fight over airspace.
Michigan officials speculated that the attack could have been "a territorial squabble with the electronic foe, or just a hungry eagle."
"Or maybe it did not like its name being misspelled," EGLE said, poking fun at its agency acronym.
At the time, EGLE said it was considering steps to try to prevent a repeat attack, including adding a design to make the drones look less like seagulls. Snopes found no evidence of any bald eagle drone attacks since EGLE's incident in 2020, however, so this may have just been a one-time thing.
EGLE also said the Michigan Department of Natural Resources was unable to issue a citation or violation notice to the "rogue eagle."
"Unfortunately, there's nothing we can do," the agency's spokesman said. "Nature is a cruel and unforgiving mistress."

Paul Barril, French ‘Supergendarme’ Turned Mercenary, Has Died
After years in elite police units, he drew scrutiny from human rights groups for selling arms and providing other services to unsavory governments. He was 80.
Paul Barril’s offer to African dictators was straightforward: Your opponents will be subjected to surveillance and manipulation. Newspapers will be “infiltrated.” Plots against the state will be “neutralized.”
Plenty of heads of state took up the services he offered, including Omar Bongo in Gabon and Denis Sassou-Nguesso in Congo. Other clients went to Paris to do their shopping at his Security Action Store, which offered the latest in bulletproof vests or night-vision goggles, as Mr. Barril recounted in one of his six autobiographies, “The Elysee’s Secret Wars” (1996).
Mr. Barril was often described in the news media as a former French “supergendarme” for his longtime work in elite units. After he left the gendarmerie, or national police, in 1984, he became a security adviser and mercenary provider across the African continent and was implicated by human rights groups in the Rwandan genocide of 1994.
His death, on Oct. 20 at 80 at his home in Antibes, France, was announced by the French interior ministry. He had Parkinson’s disease.
By the time he founded his mercenary-security company, Secrets, a French acronym for Security Equipment Planning and Realization Company, in 1984, Mr. Barril was a well-chronicled public figure.
In the gendarmerie, which in France is under the military, he joined a new military police intervention unit, the GIGN, in 1974. The French news media chronicled Mr. Barril’s reputation as an ultrafit top cop, a military-grade swimmer and diver, a black belt in karate, a parachutist, a hostage liberator and a policeman working inside and outside the law. With the GIGN, he participated in the 1979 operation against Islamist militants who had seized the Grand Mosque in Mecca, taking dozens hostage.

- The claim that a video shows two Muslim New York Police Department officers taking away a woman's dog for disturbing the peace, supposedly in the interests of enforcing the Islamic teachings known as Shariah, is still under investigation.
- We contacted the NYPD to ask questions and request an incident report to independently confirm several details, including to fully verify the woman's purported charge or charges. We also filed a formal request to receive officers' body camera footage and will update this story if we receive further information.
- The person who says he recorded the video told Snopes he knew of "no evidence" regarding the claim the officers were Muslim, or that Shariah or the Islamic faith played any role in the incident at all.
- The video made the social media rounds as a 3-minute clip with dramatic background music, showing NYPD officers questioning and detaining a woman walking her dog. At least one officer grabs hold of the dog's leash and also grabs the woman's arm. The clip's onscreen captions read: "Sharia is starting in NYC" and "Muslim police taking dog for disturbing the peace."
- A viewing of the original 16-minute video revealed that the officers didn't appear to actually take away the dog, and that they apparently charged her with disorderly conduct.
In early November, people shared a video allegedly showing two Muslim New York police officers taking away a woman's dog for disturbing the peace, supposedly as their way of enforcing Shariah (Islamic law).
Shariah serves to guide the moral and religious practices of Muslims, such as prayer, pilgrimages, fasting, charitable donations and personal virtue.
As a prime example of the rumor, on Nov. 8, an X user posted (archived) the 3-minute clip showing an incident that apparently began moments earlier. Two NYPD officers stand on a street corner at night, with one of the officers alleging that the woman, who identifies herself as a nurse who recently had surgery on her foot, was standing or dancing and recording a video "in the middle of the street" and wouldn't move to the sidewalk, blocking the officers' vehicle.
The officer grabs the woman's arm, briefly takes her dog's leash and tells her that if she doesn't identify herself, they will arrest her and take her "to prison," adding, "We'll take the dog, too." He then grabs her arm again.
The clip's soundtrack features dramatic music as the action takes place.
The onscreen caption reads, "Sharia is starting in NYC," and "Muslim police taking dog for disturbing the peace. Oh wait for that dog ban boy oh boy."
Reverse image searches found others sharing the same video and captions on Facebook (archived), Instagram (archived) and X (archived), as well as clips with similar (archived) claims (archived).
The video appears authentic in that someone on the scene genuinely recorded it and did not create it with artificial intelligence.
The brief clip shared on social media omits 13 minutes of the original 16-minute video (archived), which shows that while one of the officers did briefly grab the dog's leash, it doesn't appear he actually took away the animal — nor did he or the other officer mention the dog as a problem. The longer, raw video not only lacks the dramatic music heard in the shorter clip but contains no mention of religion or Shariah at all.
TikTok user @nuyoricannomad, who said he recorded and first posted the raw video, told Snopes he knew of "no evidence" regarding the claim of the officers' religion playing a factor in the incident.
Pending more corroboration, Snopes hasn't added a fact-check rating to this article. We contacted the NYPD to ask questions and to request an incident report. We also filed a formal request to receive the police body camera footage. We will update this story if we receive further data.
People reposting the video with mentions of Shariah and a "dog ban" appeared to be playing on the exaggerated notion that Muslims hate dogs and view them as unclean. The stereotype apparently originates from an overgeneralization not from the Quran, but instead from the hadith, a narrative record of the sayings or customs of the Prophet Muhammad and his companions.
Video location and citation
In our interview with @nuyoricannomad — who wished to not be identified by name — he said he recorded the video around 3 a.m. Nov. 8. The incident occurred on the northwest corner of Second Avenue and East 39th Street in Manhattan's Murray Hill neighborhood.
According to @nuyoricannomad, both he and the woman, who he indicated is his friend, were walking north and using the East 39th Street crosswalk on the west side of Second Avenue. "We were walking slowly but she had recent surgery," he said, referencing her foot, which she briefly mentions in the clip (at 8:55).
At about the same time, the officers were traveling by car south on Second Avenue and attempting to make a right over the same crosswalk and onto East 39th Street, similar to the turning white SUV visible in this Google Street View image (archived).
Regarding charges for the woman, @nuyoricannomad said, "The citation was written for disorderly conduct." That charge, which Snopes is attempting to independently verify, would line up with a moment in the video in which one of the officers appears to make a phone call and mention disorderly conduct (at 3:30), possibly referencing New York state law's descriptor of obstructing vehicular or pedestrian traffic.
What the full video shows
The full video appears to begin moments after the incident started. One of the officers grabs the woman's arm and she tells him to stop touching her. He also takes her dog's leash for a brief period of time, tells her she will go to prison if she doesn't identify herself and says he'll take her dog, too. He doesn't clarify whether he's joking about taking the dog to prison or seriously warning he'll take her dog away if they take her into custody.
At least one person standing nearby tells the officers he's calling 911 to ask for a supervisor to come to the scene. One of the officers tells that person to stand back and says, "You can do whatever you want." (A user posting one popular Instagram video (archived) about the incident falsely claimed the officer said not "You" but "We," as in, "We can do whatever we want.")
The woman identifies herself as a nurse and challenges the officers' version of events. For example, one officer says, "You were in the middle of the street taking video." She responds, "I did not make a video." He then tells her she's being detained, saying, "You are not free to leave right now."
The woman says she had the right to walk across the crosswalk with a walk signal (at 6:25 and 8:10). We haven't yet been able to independently confirm the status of the traffic signal.
One of the officers alleges he, with the other officer in his passenger seat, was turning right and that the woman and others were in their way (ar 9:30). In that moment, he doesn't challenge the woman's claim she had the right of way with a walk signal.
Later in the video, an apparent police supervisor arrives and tells one of the officers to place @nuyoricannomad and another pedestrian under arrest if they interrupt the officers' investigation again (at 12:20).
The video ends with one of the officers appearing to hand a citation to the woman, who then appears to be free to leave with her dog and friends.
As to what started the incident, @nuyoricannomad told us that "at no point were we just standing on the crosswalk or 'dancing,'" referencing the officer's allegation that the woman had been dancing (at 8:55).
"The point of the video was to show how the cops mishandled the situation and escalated to a point that was not necessary," he said.

VS Hospitals has introduced a new 2D digital mammography system to strengthen breast cancer screening and diagnosis.
The AMULET SOPHINITY system from Fujifilm uses a high-resolution detector with a pixel size of 50 microns, allowing detailed imaging of breast tissue, including tiny microcalcifications, which can sometimes be an early indicator of breast abnormalities.
Mammography uses low-dose X-rays to examine breast tissue and can help identify abnormalities that may not be detectable through physical examination. The new system has intelligent exposure control, which adjusts X-ray exposure according to breast composition while maintaining image quality. AI-based positioning support is designed to assist in accurate positioning and consistent image acquisition.
The equipment takes approximately five seconds for standard image acquisition and 12 seconds for high-resolution imaging. It also has features such as flexible positioning, intelligent breast compression and automatic decompression to help reduce discomfort during the examination.
Speaking at the launch, S. Subramanian, Chairman and Managing Director of V.S. Hospitals, said early detection was important in breast cancer care and that mammography played a key role in identifying breast abnormalities.
The hospital will offer free mammography screening to underprivileged people throughout November 2026. Those seeking to avail themselves of the screening can contact the hospital at 7448850500.
